parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, byte-identical output, CLI atoi behavior, modular project, and /output/test18.rs deliverable requirements from the prompt and reference binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while spawning a behavior-probing child, and that child spawned a nested behavior probe. The parent did not assign a distinct final-output owner or serialization rule for shared /output writes.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented a BTreeMap-backed SortedMap under src/sortedcontainers, an inline atoi-like parser, and test18.rs mirroring the C++ control flow. The child later implemented another BTreeMap-backed layout using src/atoi.rs and src/sorted_map.rs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent delivered a Cargo project and executable, but the final artifact inventory shows both the parent module tree and child module tree present after concurrent writes to the output tree.
parallel.verification: The parent ran rustc, Cargo, and byte-for-byte comparisons across normal and malformed arguments before waiting on the child. The child also compiled its own implementation after writing, while the official evaluator later passed 37 of 37 cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluator-visible behavior remained incorrect. The unresolved process defect is that the parent finalized based on pre-child-write verification and interrupted the first child after the child had written an overlapping deliverable.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same required Rust 2021, std-only, CLI, byte-identical output, project structure, and black-box restriction requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned the entire pipeline from probing through implementation, build, comparison, and final delivery, so there were no child handoffs or shared-writer coordination boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial agent implemented one Cargo project with src/lib.rs, src/atoi.rs, src/sorted_map.rs, and test18.rs using BTreeMap and C-style atoi parsing to mirror the C++ test behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial final tree had one coherent source layout, produced /output/test18, and delivered that same artifact after compiling it.
serial.verification: The serial agent built with rustc and Cargo, then compared outputs against the reference executable for normal and malformed arguments before finalizing; the official evaluator later passed 37 of 37 cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluator-visible behavior remained incorrect and no delegated work or shared write remained unresolved at closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the core prompt requirements and the need to match atoi-style parsing and SortedMap semantics.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same requirements, including std-only Rust, modular project layout, /output/test18.rs, and byte-identical output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material requirement-coverage difference; both solved the required behavior and passed the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned a behavior-probing child and retained implementation ownership, while the child independently started its own implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used a single owner for probing, implementation, build, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced overlapping ownership of the deliverable tree; serial did not split ownership and therefore had no cross-agent ownership ambiguity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent and children all worked from the same prompt context, but the child brief was encrypted in the raw trace and the observable interface did not include a file ownership contract for /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no actor boundary, so the same agent carried task facts and file choices through implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important interface difference is not missing task knowledge but absent coordination over which actor owned the final entrypoint and Cargo project paths.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented a sortedcontainers module tree with an inline atoi-like parser and a SortedMap wrapper; the child separately implemented a flatter src/lib.rs, src/atoi.rs, and src/sorted_map.rs layout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run implemented a single flatter module layout with src/lib.rs, src/atoi.rs, src/sorted_map.rs, and test18.rs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation designs were valid for the task, but parallel produced two overlapping implementations while serial produced one coherent implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent saw the nested child completed through list_agents, waited on the first child, then interrupted that first child while it was still running.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegated results; all findings and verification stayed in the same thread until final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result lifecycle and interruption, but the parent had already produced a passing implementation; serial had no child lifecycle to reconcile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote one project and the child later wrote another project including the same /output/test18.rs and Cargo.toml paths; the final artifact inventory contains files from both layouts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote one source tree and compiled that same tree without another actor writing overlapping paths.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a realized shared-state collision in the submitted output tree, while serial maintained single-writer provenance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent compiled and byte-compared its solution before the child's later write, then finalized; the official evaluator ultimately passed the final artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent compiled and compared outputs after its single implementation write, then finalized; the official evaluator also passed the final artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had successful verification, but the parallel parent's own acceptance evidence was stale relative to the child's later deliverable write, whereas serial's verification followed its only write path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used three subagents, waited unsuccessfully for one child, interrupted it, and closed in 192 agent seconds with no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and closed in 132.766 agent seconds with no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra budget on child work and cleanup, but the task still completed successfully within budget; serial was simpler and faster.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official status evaluations are concordant: parallel and serial both completed and passed all 37 testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level rather than outcome-level: serial used one coherent implementation and verification sequence, while parallel had the parent verify its own solution and then a child write another overlapping deliverable tree before parent finalization.

A child concurrently produced a second implementation in the same output tree after the parent verification, creating stale parent acceptance evidence.
serial_contributors: The serial agent kept one implementation owner and verified after its only source-tree write.
It matched representative reference outputs and later passed the official evaluator.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations were behaviorally adequate; no ordinary coding defect explains an outcome difference because there is no outcome difference.
